column2: Was this... really for the best...?
I think it probably was...
A city built on unchecked development and reckless construction will fall apart sooner or later.
Still, it was a whole lot better than the other towns...
Of course it was for the best!
A life where you cannot do anything unless someone orders you to is wrong!
But still... it was a whole lot better than the others.
But now that we have brought about such harsh results,
you must surely have some method that you consider ideal.
It is easy to criticize someone else's methods without offering an alternative.
But if that is all you can think, there is no point in risking your life on this journey!
Yes, each city has problems of its own,
but those are problems the people who live there must solve with their own hands.
Perhaps the wisest thing is to leave this place without saying another word...
In any case, someday each person must
find with their own hands the future they believe is best.
Could everyone be $$平等$$,
and yet each person be $$自由$$...? Is that impossible?!
Unless we change the nature of this $$世界$$, it will be difficult...
To do that, we must meet the ruler of this $$世界$$,
the $$教皇$$ of the $$アンゲルス教$$, at all costs!
The moment is almost here!
According to $$ケルビム$$, once we pass through this city,
the $$総本山$$ where the $$教皇$$ resides is just ahead.
I can feel strength naturally filling the hand that writes my $$日記$$!!
I'd like to see someday
whose name is written in that revenge $$日記$$...
...Hey!
Whose face are you looking at while you write that $$日記$$?!
I see. So that is the conclusion you have reached.
That thought, action, and decisiveness...
Though only in theory, there is a strong possibility they are the people I seek...
Hey, haven't we picked up someone else?!
Let's see. One, two, three... Oh, you're right! Who are you?
I'm $$ミニオン$$. It looked fun, so I came along!
Hee hee!!
Don't "hee hee" me. Go home already!!
Aww, can't I come with you?
Sure!!
No!
Yay! I did it!
$$ミニオン$$ joined the party!!
Fine, so there! Bleeeh!
Good grief...
